criteria.descriptor: Correctly describes the trace/span model: a per-request trace, nested spans per step timed independently, trace_id/parent span_id correlation and context propagation, and accurate per-span attributes (durations, inputs/outputs, token usage, status/errors). Full marks require no incorrect claims (e.g. does not conflate tracing with aggregate metrics or with merely more verbose logs) and correct use of terms like span, trace, and attribute.

Covers both diagnostic goals: captures per-span timing/tokens for the latency problem AND per-span inputs/outputs (retrieval docs+scores, prompt, completion) for the correctness problem, plus status/errors and metadata. Full marks also mention a concrete backend/standard and the export/overhead consideration (async export or sampling).

Explicitly ties each captured field to what it lets you diagnose -- e.g. span durations localize the 8s, retrieved doc scores vs prompt vs completion distinguish a retrieval failure from a prompt or model failure -- rather than listing fields without connecting them to the two reported problems.
Explanation is well organized (clear tracing-vs-logging contrast, a legible span hierarchy, and a structured per-span capture list), uses correct vocabulary, and stays within a focused length.

expected_answer_points: A trace represents one end-to-end request and is composed of nested spans (one per step) that are individually timed, versus a single flat log line -- so per-step latency and structure become visible
Spans are correlated via a shared trace_id and parent span_id (context propagation across steps/async/service boundaries), letting you reconstruct the full request tree/waterfall

Capture inputs and outputs per span -- retrieval: query plus returned doc ids/scores/count; LLM: rendered prompt/messages and the completion -- which is what lets you diagnose WHY an answer was wrong (bad retrieval vs bad prompt vs model)
Capture timing/duration on every span, plus token usage/cost on LLM spans, to isolate the source of the 8s latency
Capture status and errors/exceptions plus metadata attributes (request id, user id, model name/version, temperature/params) on spans
Name a concrete standard/tool and export path -- LangSmith, Langfuse, or OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions to a collector -- that renders a span waterfall UI
Address overhead/safety: asynchronous export and/or sampling to limit latency impact, and redaction of PII in captured prompts/outputs
common_pitfalls: Proposes just adding more or more verbose log lines (e.g. a log per step) instead of a hierarchical trace with correlated parent/child spans, so the answer never gains the structure that localizes the failing step
Captures only latency/durations and omits per-span inputs/outputs, so the slow step can be found but the wrong-answer cause cannot (or vice versa -- captures prompts but no timing)
Confuses tracing with aggregate metrics/dashboards (Prometheus counters, average latency), which cannot drill into a single bad request
Forgets trace_id/span_id correlation and context propagation, so spans cannot be stitched into one request across the tool call or async boundaries
Dumps full prompts/completions with no mention of PII redaction, cost/volume, or that export/sampling has overhead -- or claims tracing every request is free
Answers with an unrelated fix (set temperature=0, switch models, add retries) instead of adding observability
reference_answer:
Flat logging gives one line per request; tracing gives one trace per request built from nested, individually-timed spans, so you can view the request as a waterfall and localize the failing or slow step instead of guessing.

Structure: a root span for the whole request carries a trace_id, with child spans for each step -- embed_query, vector_search, prompt_build, llm_call_1, tool_call, llm_call_2. Each span records start/end (duration), status, and its parent span_id, so the tree reconstructs the exact execution path. The trace context propagates across async boundaries and any service hops so spans stitch into one request.

Per-span capture:
- All spans: name, duration, status (ok/error), recorded exceptions, and attributes like request id, user id, and model/version.
- Retrieval span: the query plus returned doc ids, similarity scores, and count -- this exposes correctness failures from bad retrieval.
- LLM spans: model name, parameters (temperature, max_tokens), the rendered prompt/messages, the completion, and token usage (prompt/completion) plus cost.
- Tool span: tool name, arguments, and result or error.

Diagnosis: the span durations in the waterfall reveal which step eats the 8s (e.g. vector_search vs generation); the captured inputs/outputs on the retrieval and LLM spans reveal why an answer was wrong -- irrelevant retrieved docs, a malformed prompt, or a model error. Export spans asynchronously to a tracing backend (LangSmith/Langfuse or an OTel collector), sample to bound overhead, and redact PII in prompts/outputs before export.
